voices.note: the mishna of 5b.7 (תנא דידן); called רבנן at 6a.7-9

props.gloss_en: the mishna: the exemption of an offspring of another species is derived from the doubled 'firstborn of a donkey'
a ewe that bore a goat of sorts, and a goat that bore a ewe of sorts, are exempt from the firstborn law
and if it has some of the signs [of its mother], it is obligated
Rav Yehuda: [the exemption] is from the verse 'but the firstborn of an ox, the firstborn of a lamb, the firstborn of a goat'
the criterion read from it: it must be an ox and its firstborn an ox; a lamb and its firstborn a lamb; a goat and its firstborn a goat
might it be [exempt] even if it has some of the signs? the verse says 'but' -- it distinguished
the stam: the tanna and R' Yosei HaGelili differ over in which sanctity the Merciful One revealed the rule
the tanna: the Merciful One revealed it in sanctity of value [the donkey], and the same holds for inherent sanctity
R' Yosei: the Merciful One revealed it in inherent sanctity, the same holds for sanctity of value, and he derives sanctity of value from inherent sanctity
the tanna needs the repeated 'firstborn' for R' Yosei b. R' Chanina's teaching
sacrificial portions are stated for a firstborn ox, for a firstborn lamb and for a firstborn goat
for RYHG: had the verse meant only the portions it would write 'the firstborn of an ox, lamb and goat'; the repeated 'firstborn' teaches that it must be an ox and its firstborn an ox

R' Yosei HaGelili needs the doubled 'firstborn of a donkey' to exclude horses and camels (after the baraita's hava aminot: 'the firstborn of an impure animal you shall redeem' would include them; and 'still I would say donkeys with a lamb, horses and camels with anything')
firstborn horses and camels are not subject to the firstborn law
Rav Pappa: the tanna's exclusion of horses and camels is from 'all your livestock... ox and lamb... and the firstborn of a donkey'
'all your livestock' is a generalisation, 'ox and lamb and donkey' a detail; generalisation and detail: the generalisation holds only what is in the detail
ox, lamb and donkey -- yes; anything else -- no
R' Yosei HaGelili: the word 'firstborn' [of a donkey] interrupts the matter -- the donkey is not in the detail
the Rabbis: the vav [of 've-peter'] joins it back in
a cow that bore a donkey of sorts with some of the signs [of its mother] is obligated -- the baraitot's 'with signs, obligated' read, by the deflections, as said of this case
(proposed) a cow that bore a horse of sorts with some signs is obligated
(proposed) a donkey that bore a horse of sorts with some signs is obligated
baraita A: a tahor animal that bore a tamei animal of sorts is exempt; if it has some of the signs, obligated
baraita B: a cow that bore a donkey of sorts and a donkey that bore a horse of sorts are exempt; if it has some of the signs, obligated
baraita B's clause: a donkey that bore a horse of sorts is exempt

תא שמע: פרה שילדה מין חמור וחמור שילדה מין סוס... מאי לאו אתרווייהו?

objections.gloss_en: והא תנא פטר פטר קנסיב לה, לפרה -- but the tanna takes [the exemption] from פטר פטר, for the cow!

answered_by.gloss_en: הוא דאמר כרבי יוסי הגלילי, דתניא -- Rav Yehuda says it like R' Yosei HaGelili (the baraita, 5b.13-14)

objections.gloss_en: ורבי יוסי הגלילי? -- [the repeated 'firstborn' is needed for the portions (5b.17-18)]

answered_by.gloss_en: אם כן ליכתוב קרא אך בכור שור כשב ועז; בכור בכור למה לי? אלא לאו ש״מ (= p_lichtov_shor_kesev_vaez)

objections.gloss_en: פריך רב אחאי: written once, it is a davar shehaya bichlal veyatza lelamed, teaching about the whole klal -- all redeemed with a lamb; the second פטר חמור excludes horses and camels from the lamb -- ואימא מעטינהו משה, ולעולם בכל דבר (6a.2-3)

answered_by.gloss_en: אם כן לכתוב רחמנא פטר חמור תפדה בשה וחמור תפדה בשה; the full repeated phrase -- פטרי חמורים אמרתי לך ולא פטרי סוסים וגמלים

objections.gloss_en: ורבי יוסי הגלילי? לא לכתוב לא וי״ו ולא פטר -- [if the donkey were in the detail] let it write neither (the stam on his behalf)

answered_by.gloss_en: ורבנן? איידי דהא קדושת דמים והא קדושת הגוף -- פסיק להו והדר עריב להו (the stam on the Rabbis' behalf)
